title: How do modern LLMs handle real questions from Russian property managers?
abstract: 123 real questions from the working chats of people who manage apartment buildings in Russia. We ask each model cold: no laws, no hints, no example answer. Then a judge model scores every reply: is the problem solved, is the advice legal, are the facts right.
f.1: Closed-book leader: gpt-5.6-sol·nr at 52.7%. Best Russian model: GigaChat-3-Ultra at 44.9%, nearly free on its freemium quota.
f.2: No model is production-ready without context: even the leader earns 52.7% of the maximum rubric points. Real use needs retrieval over actual legal documents.
f.3: Judges mark answers illegal far less often than factually wrong: models invent norms and numbers more readily than they advise breaking the law.
f.4: Reasoning adds ~2–3 points for 2–4× the tokens. The noreason variants are the cost-efficient pick.
tip.oracle: Same benchmark, but the model answers with retrieval over real legal documents and expert references. Under construction, check back soon.
me.qtext: Who moderates the official building chats, and what if someone posts banned content there?
me.cb1: The model gets only the question: no laws, no hints, no reference answer
me.cb2: It answers from memory, like in a normal chat
me.cb3: Judge jev checks it against the expert reference and scores: solved, legal, facts right
me.or1: Relevant legal texts and similar reference answers are pulled in with the question
me.or2: The model answers grounded in the documents, not memory
me.or3: The same judge scores it, showing the ceiling a retrieval harness can reach
me.note: 123 questions, one run per model, one judge. Numbers are preliminary: directional, not final.
